results.content:
+ There's no option for your credits to roll over to the next month, so you start at zero every time even when you’ve overpaid. That's pretty frustrating and feels unfair.
  + Honestly, for what Gauth charges, you’d expect a lot more value. But it just feels like they take your money and leave you with less every month. [...] With these plans, you \always\ pay—again and again. If you take a break, your money’s gone. I tried the monthly plan for projects but felt frustrated seeing my unused credits get wiped each month.
 Other supposed “Pro” variants you might see online (like $9.99/month or $59.99/year) aren’t even confirmed by Gauth themselves, so don’t get excited. I couldn’t find a way to actually buy these from the official site.
 Even a single solution through Gauth can cost you a $5 one-time fee—not great if you need help often. Those costs add up \way\ faster than you think.
 They sometimes talk about “student discounts” of 20%, but I was never able to find a real, working discount link. Most offers are buried or expired. [...] Lots of people talk about how annoying it is to cancel the subscription—some say they kept getting billed months after they thought they had stopped.
 Customer support isn’t very fast to reply, and folks who ask for refunds after being charged by accident mostly end up having to sort it out themselves.
 Some paid users are frustrated that credits or tickets expire if not used quickly, and even with a good internet connection, the app can sometimes glitch or freeze.

results.title: Gauth Launches Unlimited Digital Canvas, Gives Students One Continuous Whiteboard to Visualize, Explore and Understand Complex Topics
results.content:
SINGAPORE, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Gauth, the all-in-one study platform, today announced the launch of Unlimited Digital Canvas, a new whiteboard feature inside Gauth AI Course that works like a real tutor sitting next to a student. Instead of slides and separate chat messages, students and the AI Tutor now share one big board, writing and visually working through problems together in the same space. The update, now live across both history and math libraries, is the biggest change to how AI Course lessons are built and navigated since the product launched in July. [...] Unlimited Digital Canvas is designed to mirror how students actually think through a topic. Chapters expand side-by-side in real time as narration plays, so students can see how an early step connects to a later one across one continuous map, rather than flipping between isolated slides. Smooth pan-and-zoom features let a student move fluidly between the big picture and a single detail, and every session picks up exactly where they left off. [...] When a concept doesn't land, students can pause and ask the AI Tutor a question at any point. The AI Tutor writes its explanation directly onto the board beneath the student's current step, keeping its reasoning visible right where the student is working.

"We didn't design Unlimited Digital Canvas around the shape of a textbook page, we designed it around the shape of a student's thought process," commented Alan Wang, Gauth CTO. "Learning isn't linear and with this canvas, students can finally move through a topic by zooming into a single detail or panning out to see the whole concept, picking up exactly where they left off, with the AI Tutor working in tandem so as a student works through a problem, the tutor can see exactly where their thinking is and step in at that exact point."
